name: Whitley Award
summary: Annual award of project funding over one year for mid-career, grassroots conservation leaders who are nationals of an eligible country and are scaling up proven, community-based, science-led work.

geography.label: Countries not classified as a High-Income Economy by the World Bank (with listed exceptions)

eligibility.rule: Be a national of the country where you work and be embedded in local communities
Work for a locally incorporated conservation charity, NGO, not-for-profit or university
Involve grassroots communities in practical action founded on science
Not a lone individual, a team entry or a joint entry
Communicate verbally in English without a translator
Demonstrate a track record of success relevant to the proposed activities
Not a government employee (staff of government-funded universities are typically eligible)
Not propose MSc or PhD work, expeditions, land purchase, building construction or animal welfare projects

documents: Registration certificate issued by the relevant regulatory authority
Financial statements/accounts including income and expenditure statement, balance sheet and audit statement or report

status.quote: Applications for the 2027 Whitley Awards are now closed. Winners will be announced at our annual ceremony in April 2027.

applicant_types.quote: Whitley Awards recognise individuals backed by an experienced team or organisation that can demonstrate past success and an evidence-based approach.

geography.quote: Eligible countries are those not classified as a High-Income Economy by the World Bank.

places.quote: COUNTRIES ELIGIBLE FOR THE 2027 WHITLEY AWARD

access.quote: You do not need to be invited or nominated to apply for a Whitley Award.

window.quote: Awarded annually, Whitley Awards recognise grassroots conservation leaders, providing funding to support and scale up proven, science-based solutions that deliver lasting impact for both people and nature.

amount.quote: Each Whitley Award is worth £50,000 in project funding over one year.

effort.quote: Complete your application online after registering on the application portal.
Applications will be reviewed in November and shortlisted candidates will be invited for interviews in January.

eligibility.quote: Grassroots conservation leaders who are nationals of the country where they work (i.e. you were born there or have lived there long term and obtained national status) and are embedded in local communities.

The organisation must be a registered charity, NGO, not-for-profit or university whose mission is the protection and conservation of biodiversity and ecosystems. It must be locally incorporated in an eligible country.
To be eligible, projects must involve communities at the grassroots level and deliver practical action that is founded on science.
Individuals working in isolation, as well as team or joint entries, are not eligible.
applicants must be able to communicate verbally in English without a translator.
Applicants must demonstrate a track record of success relevant to the proposed activities, with appropriate metrics and baseline data.

Government employees. However, we recognise that some conservationists are affiliated with government institutions as part of their work. For example, applicants employed by government-funded universities are typically eligible.
WFN cannot provide funding for MSc/ PhD work, expeditions, land purchase, building construction, or animal welfare projects.

documents.quote: a Microsoft Word template for your logical framework/timeline, and a Microsoft Excel template for your budget
Organisation's founding documents (e.g. constitution, registration certificate) with an English translation if available. Registration certificate issued by the relevant regulatory authority.

This can be provided in one or multiple documents, but it must include an income and expenditure statement, a balance sheet and an audit statement or report signed by an independent external auditor. Organisational bank account details used to receive funds if your application is successful.
Please ensure that all three statements are submitted to us via the portal before the deadline so that they can be considered with your application.
